issue_context.title: `experimental-specifier-resolution=node` doesn't resolve realpath
issue_context.body:
### Version

v17.6.0

### Platform

Darwin VMBP2021.local 21.2.0 Darwin Kernel Version 21.2.0: Sun Nov 28 20:28:41 PST 2021; root:xnu-8019.61.5~1/RELEASE_ARM64_T6000 arm64

### Subsystem

esm resolver

### What steps will reproduce the bug?

https://github.com/vjpr/issue-node-experimental-specifier-resolution

```
pnpm install
./index.sh
```

### How often does it reproduce? Is there a required condition?

Pnpm relies on realpaths. Package managers relying on hoisting will not encounter this issue as they will eventually find the package hoisted.

This is why it was probably hard to detect.

### What is the expected behavior?

Realpath should be called when `--experimental-specifier-resolution=node` is set.

### What do you see instead?

It's not being called, and modules are resolved using logical paths.

### Additional information

https://github.com/nodejs/node/blame/e5c1fd7a2a1801fd75bdde23b260488e85453eb2/lib/internal/modules/esm/resolve.js#L367-L410

Notice how `realpathSync` is not called if the `--experimental-specifier-resolution=node` option is set.

review_comments: So it seems like the significant change here is to remove the `return` statements from the above code and instead set the resolved file to the `path` variable, which gets further attention related to symlinks below? Yet there’s also a check that the resolved `path` isn’t a directory, which makes sense for ESM resolution but not for the legacy CommonJS style; though by that point any “directory” imports would have been resolved to `<whatever>/index.js`, I assume?

I checked that there is a chance to return a directory (when the path ends with `/` and `resolveDirectoryEntry` return undefined):

https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/29bb2bb57d2a993e4e79172fe6b954f8047eee81/lib/internal/modules/esm/resolve.js#L381-L386

And it seems to be added explicitly:
https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/f8976a76bbb49d678056d6d2ddd57064cf9e63c2#diff-b4c24f634e3741e5ad9e8c29864a48f2bd284a9d66d8fed3d077ccee0c44087bR253

I will follow this and jump the check below, only process symlinks.

Can anyone remember the use case of return `resolved` (which is a directory that ends with `/`) directly?
https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/29bb2bb57d2a993e4e79172fe6b954f8047eee81/lib/internal/modules/esm/resolve.js#L385

I can add a test case for that.
i mean, a path of `./foo/` could be `./foo/index`, or the "main" in `./foo/package.json` - is that what you mean?

This is handled by `resolveDirectoryEntry`.
What I wonder is the case: if `./foo/index` etc. not found, the origin `resolved` (which in case is `./foo/`) is returned.

But anyway, I kept this behavior unchanged in the latest commit, only handling file's symlink.

I’m not sure I follow. My question is whether this breaks directory imports. Previously, the `node` mode never got down to the `resolveDirectoryEntry` logic because of the `return`s that this PR removes. Now the `node` mode does go through that block (that begins with `if (stats.isDirectory()) {`), so my question is, is this okay? I assume it is, because by the time it gets there, any specifiers of `'./folder'` have been resolved to `'./folder/index.js'`; but can you confirm that I’m correct here?

If so, we have nothing to worry about and this is fine to merge in; but if I’m wrong, we’ll need to address this case somehow.

This change will not break directory imports.

`resolveExtensionsWithTryExactName` and `resolveDirectoryEntry` will return either a file or undefined, and will never return a directory.

If `resolveExtensionsWithTryExactName` return a file,
- before the change: it will return directly
- after the change: it will go through `isDerectory()` and `!isFile()` (which is ok) and `realpathSync` (which is we want)

If `resolveExtensionsWithTryExactName` return undefined,
- before the change: it will call `resolveDirectoryEntry` and try to find the file from package.json, if the path ends with '/' and a file is not found, it will return a dirctory.
- after the change: it will behave the same as before, then
  - if the path ends with '/' and a file is not found, it will return a directory directly.
  - if the path is not undefined (in this case, can be sure is a file), it will go through `isDerectory()` and `!isFile()` (which is ok) and `realpathSync` (which is we want).
